champion: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum-like disorder with multiple coagulation factor deficiency
ordered_diagnoses: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum-like disorder with multiple coagulation factor deficiency

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive skin laxity with flexural papules and calcification of elastic fibers
salient_findings: Asymptomatic yellowish coalesced papules in flexural areas
Severe skin sagging with loss of elasticity
Excessive calcification of elastic fiber fragments in the reticular dermis
key_facts: 20-year history of progressive skin laxity
Asymptomatic yellowish coalesced papules in flexural areas since early childhood
Severe skin sagging occurred on the abdomen with loss of elasticity
Skin symptoms spread extensively with developmental growth
No extracutaneous involvement
Born to healthy nonconsanguineous parents
Younger sister had developed the same skin symptoms
Low clotting activity of factor X (52.2%)
Prolonged prothrombin time (12.8 seconds)
Echocardiographic examination results were normal
Fundoscopic examination results were normal
Histopathology showed excessive calcification of elastic fiber fragments in the reticular dermis
Genetic testing revealed compound heterozygous sequence variation in GGCX gene

shortlist.label: Cutis laxa

shortlist.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: While less likely, some forms of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome can present with skin laxity and joint hypermobility, although the latter is not mentioned in the case

shortlist.label: Gerodermia osteodysplastica
shortlist.why_kept: This rare disorder can present with skin laxity and skeletal abnormalities, although the latter is not mentioned in the case

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of progressive skin laxity, yellowish coalesced papules, and severe skin sagging, combined with the laboratory findings of low clotting activity of factor X and prolonged prothrombin time, and the genetic testing revealing compound heterozygous sequence variation in the GGCX gene, are most consistent with this diagnosis.
